answer=3 raw="<think>An impermeable wall means no fluid can pass through it. The condition for an impermeable wall is that the velocity component normal to the wall is zero at the surface. This is expressed as V·n = 0 at the surface.

The flow isn't zero at the wall (tangential flow can exist - no-slip says tangential velocity is zero, but the impermeability condition only requires normal velocity to be zero). So option 2 is too restrictive.

The condition applies at the surface, not above it. So option 4 is wrong.

Option 3 is correct: V·n = 0 at the surface.

Option 1 is wrong because velocity isn't zero above the surface - flow exists above the wall.</think>
